LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 23, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:53 p.m. on March
23, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll*
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout
City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to submit live
comments via Zoom; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
on all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded
to the City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  March 23, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Kim led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Kyung Lee from Saddleback Church Irvine provided the invocation.

  MOMENT OF SILENCE

  Mayor Khan asked for a Moment of Silence in memory of the victims of the Boulder and
  Atlanta shootings.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Update on Taking Action to Support a Diverse and Tolerant
  Community

  Melissa Haley, Deputy City Manager, and Michael Kent, Assistant
  Chief of Police, presented the staff report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning the timeline for rolling
  out forms to report hate crimes and incidents; inquired about whether
  the website and forms for reporting hate crimes and incidents would
  be available in multiple languages; and suggested that the form for
  reporting hate crimes and incidents be placed on the City’s main
  webpage.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the City’s efforts to
  support a diverse and tolerant community:

  Jen Chiou, Irvine resident
  Melisa Masri, Irvine resident

  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident, and Alejandro, also spoke in support of the
  City’s efforts to support a diverse and tolerant community, and in
  support of a reduction in police funding.

  Gary Flora, Irvine resident, expressed concern about threats to white
  Americans, and spoke in opposition to defunding the police.

  Received and filed. No action was taken.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 23, 2021

  1.2  Presentation by CalVet on the Process and Timeline of the
  Veteran’s Cemetery

  Prior to the presentation, Mayor Khan noted that the City had received
  a letter from an attorney on behalf of concerned Irvine residents
  pertaining to potential conflicts of interest related to Councilmember
  Agran and the Veteran’s Cemetery.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, provided a brief summary of the concerns
  referenced in the letter, noting that he had not had an opportunity to
  fully review the document as it had just recently been received; and
  further noted that he had a responsibility under the City’s Municipal
  Code to review all matters related to the Ethic Ordinance and Ethical
  Public Services Ordinance, and would consult with the FPPC as
  necessary.

  Councilmember Agran noted that he had not been made aware of the
  letter, and that no conflicts of interest nor any type of impropriety had
  occurred.

  Dave Gerard, Chief Facilities and Business Services Division of the
  California Department of Veterans Affairs (CALVET), provided an
  update on the veteran’s cemetery feasibility study and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included: noting correspondence received
  from Senator Tom Umberg related to the Veteran’s Cemetery
  (Cemetery); inquired about the completion of the feasibility study, and
  whether the City could move forward prior to its completion; requested
  clarification with respect to federal and state regulations and
  requirements; discussed the different sites, development and
  remediation costs, and potential state and federal funding/grants for
  design and construction costs; questioned which sites were being
  studied by CalVet; noted the City Council’s adoption of the initiative
  petition on May 12, 2020, selecting the Amended and Restated
  Development and Agreement (ARDA) site as the preferred site for the
  Cemetery; discussed next steps; requested clarification of zoning
  exemptions related to City-owned property; inquired as to whether the
  golf course could be rezoned for the Cemetery if transferred to the
  State; reiterated that Assembly Bill 368 specifically called for the study
  on both the ARDA and the golf course sites; and noted that the City
  was bound by State law to allow CalVet to complete the study.

  City Attorney Melching clarified provisions of the City’s Zoning Code
  and exemptions for City- and State-owned property of such
  requirements, as well as language contained in the initiative with
  respect to internal inconsistences.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3

  714-***-*900, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the completion of the
  CalVet study.

  Katrina Stanchfield and Eric Hildebran, Irvine residents, spoke in

  GLFSR, inquired about which entity would determine site selection,
  and whether costs associated with pre-construction were available for

  Received and filed. No action was taken.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  March 23, 2021

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo provided a brief summary of his recent meeting with State Senator
  Ming regarding local school districts, concerns raised by residents related to the All
  American Asphalt plant, green building within the City of Irvine, and pending Regional
  Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) guidelines and statistics. He also announced that
  he was recently selected as the president of the Irvine Community Land Trust.

  Councilmember Carroll announced that he and Mayor Khan were participants in a
  subgroup that met with senior representatives from University of California, Irvine
  (UCI), and that a settlement had been reached regarding UCI medical building
  construction, mitigation fees, and a plan to build additional housing.

  Mayor Khan wished members of the community a Happy Nowruz; made the following
  announcements:

  •  March 26 is “Social Emotional Learning Day.” The Emotional Learning Alliance
  for California is a group that empowers youths to thrive in school and lives by
  advancing and supporting culturally responsive social and emotional learning
  program, policies, and practices.

  •  The City’s Disability Services team received the organization’s 2021 Community
  Partner Spotlight Award from the Regional Center of Orange County for its efforts
  to provide inclusive virtual social and recreation programs to individuals with
  disabilities. After the City’s Sweet Shade Ability Center closed due to COVID-19
  restrictions, Disability Services staff developed a virtual activity program to keep
  participants engaged by leading more than 140 online classes in yoga, art,
  cooking, and life skills, and held a Drive-thru Winter Festival.

  •  Runners, walkers, and animal lovers were invited to participate in the Irvine
  Animal Care Center Virtual 5K throughout the month of April to support animals
  in need. This year’s event also celebrated the City’s 50th anniversary. Special
  “5K + 50” bonus activities will be announced through social media during April,
  giving participants the chance to share what they love about Irvine and the Irvine
  Animal Care Center. Registration opens this week at irvineanimals.org/5k, and
  residents have through April 30th to complete the race. Participants are able to
  enter their four-legged friend to participate. Proceeds will be used to support the
  shelter and care for animals, including licensing for Irvine residents, pet
  adoptions, and events.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  March 23, 2021

  •  March 17, 2021, marked one year since the City issued a local emergency
  proclamation and took additional steps to protect the community amid the
  COVID-19 pandemic. City staff worked hard to adapt programs and services so
  that the City could safely do business and stay connected as a community. Many
  residents and businesses have shown kindness and compassion, and have
  taken action to prevent COVID-19 in Irvine.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  2) Proclaimed April 2021 as "DMV/Donate Life California

  3) Ratified and Proclaimed March 21, 2021, as "World Down

  4) In Recognition of Turkish National Sovereignty and

  5) Proclaimed April 2021 as "Sexual Assault Awareness

  2.4  BUDGET ADJUSTMENT FOR ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK
  TENNIS PROGRAM

  ACTION:
  Approved a Great Park budget adjustment to increase revenues
  by $293,341 and expenditures by $229,281 in Fiscal Year 2020-

  (Unless otherwise directed by a member of the City Council, the

  2.6  FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 SECOND QUARTER BUDGET UPDATE

  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident, expressed concern with fund allocations

  Stephen Coffey, Irvine resident, expressed concern with the City’s

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, clarified that there were

  3.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  3.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND DIRECTION TO DIRECTOR

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager, presented the staff

  There was no City Council discussion

  Pamela Wykoff, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the approximate

  Kyler Chin and Stephen Coffey, Irvine residents, spoke in support of
  funding to fight white supremacy and community programs; and in

  Received and filed. No action was taken.

  3.2  ATHLETIC FEE REDUCTIONS AND BUDGET ADJUSTMENT

  Steve Stewart, Community Services Superintendent, presented the
  staff report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about the fiscal impact
  associated with providing a full fee waiver for Irvine residents, and
  partial fee waiver for non-Irvine residents, and decreasing fees until the
  fall of 2021; and noted the negative impacts on youth sports
  organization related to the lack of normal playing and participation time.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  8
